verdict.rationale: DBOS's docs and quickstart explicitly describe checkpointing workflow/step state to Postgres and resuming from the last completed step after a crash, restart, or interruption, with a live demo ('crash the app... watch it seamlessly recover'). Community corroboration (HN threads) confirms the core durable-execution mechanism (log-then-replay via Postgres) and even highlights production use cases (Kafka exactly-once pipelines), though one critique notes recovery guarantees are only as strong as Postgres's own durability settings (e.g., async replication could lose a step). Missing for 10: independent hands-on benchmark specifically verifying full state recovery after an actual infra failure, and clearer guidance on configuring Postgres durability to match the claimed guarantee.
